A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

our analysis of the data sets provides a data driven receptor type model, with a set of chemical components that are physically meaningful, and can be used to describe aerosol composition in a site specific way.
the presented analysis provides an improved, data driven receptor model, capable of explaining a significant fraction of aerosol mass, with a high degree of chemical specificity.

the combined statistical analysis of mass spectra from a mass spectrometer is an effective way to construct a data driven model for aerosol chemical composition, which can explain most of the variability in the measured data, and which can provide a more robust and comprehensive description of the aerosol composition than more traditional, simplistic methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the aerosol chemical composition at the site is complex, and that a simple inorganic apportionment is not enough to capture the aerosol chemical diversity and variability.
the aerosol chemical mass balance can be significantly enhanced by using all available information in the data, and by employing statistical methods in a synergistic way.

the combined use of statistical analysis tools can be used to construct data driven chemical mass balances, capable of describing the chemical composition of atmospheric aerosol in a more robust and comprehensive manner than traditional approaches.
